Bank holiday today: Are SBI, HDFC, ICICI, PNB and other banks open or closed on Saturday, November 14, 2026? Check RBI calendar here
sum: Bank holiday today: Planning a bank visit today? You might need to reschedule. Bank customers planning to visit SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Punjab National Bank and other branches for cash deposits, cheque clearances or updating passbooks on November 14, 2026, are advised to check the calendar in advance before stepping out.

However, digital banking services remain fully functional on all days irrespective of branch operations. Customers can use the internet and mobile banking services, withdraw cash from ATMs and make payments using UPI. Daily digital transactions continue without any disruption.
As November 14, 2026, falls on the second Saturday of the month therefore all the private and public-sector banks across India will remain closed today.

Under the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) banking holiday rules, all scheduled and non-scheduled banks remain closed on the second and fourth Saturdays, while other Saturdays are regular working days unless a separate state-specific holiday has been declared.

The Reserve Bank of India decides the bank holidays in India. It publishes the RBI bank holiday calendar at the beginning of every year. Bank holidays are followed as per the RBI bank holiday calendar.

There are usually two types of bank holidays which include national holidays and government holidays. The government holidays are categorised into two: state government holidays and central government holidays.
Bank holidays vary from region to region, depending on the festivals and observances. However, all banks observe holidays on national holidays like Republic Day and Gandhi Jayanti.

HDFC Bank shares stage a comeback, rally over 12% in 1 month; has India's largest private lender finally escaped its valuation trap?
sum: Акции HDFC Bank за месяц подскочили более чем на 12 процентов, но опасения по поводу оценок все еще сохраняются. Citi прогнозирует потенциал роста на 16 процентов, поскольку аналитик оценивает перспективы роста компании.

После падения почти на 20 процентов в 2026 году акции HDFC Bank, крупнейшего кредитора частного сектора Индии, похоже, начинают восстанавливаться, прибавив более 12 процентов за последний месяц. Тем не менее, поскольку акции восстанавливаются с недавних минимумов, инвесторы хотят знать, есть ли у ралли дальнейшее развитие и остается ли HDFC Bank привлекательной возможностью для покупки на текущих уровнях.

В своем последнем сообщении глобальная брокерская фирма Citi повысила целевую цену акций HDFC Bank на 7 процентов до 940 рупий с 880 рупий. Пересмотренная цель предполагает потенциал роста примерно на 16 процентов по сравнению с текущей рыночной ценой акций в 812,30 рупий.
Вторя аналогичному мнению, Кранти Батини, директор по стратегии акций WealthMills Securities, сказал: «Акции (HDFC Bank) могут вырасти с этого уровня также на 10–15 процентов. У них есть потенциал».

Пересмотренная целевая цена акций Citi сигнализирует о позитивном прогнозе по банковским акциям, предполагая, что недавнее восстановление может иметь дальнейшее развитие. Однако инвесторам необходимо будет оценить основную причину брокерской деятельности и перспективы роста банка, прежде чем принимать инвестиционное решение.

Одним из ключевых факторов, поддерживающих позитивный прогноз Citi, является ожидание 15-процентного роста кредитования в 27 финансовом году. Брокерская компания ожидает, что рост будет обеспечен за счет малого и среднего бизнеса, а также необеспеченного розничного сегмента.

Citi также рассматривает восстановление рентабельности капитала (ROE) до уровня выше 15 процентов в качестве ключевого среднесрочного приоритета для банка, особенно после снижения прибыльности после слияния.

HDFC Bank stock gets shareholder mandate for Bagchi CEO term
sum: HDFC Bank shareholders approved Anup Bagchi as the bank's managing director and chief executive officer in a postal ballot concluded on Friday, November 6, 2026. The result gives the incoming leadership a formal shareholder mandate after the Reserve Bank of India had approved the appointment and related terms.

The resolution passed with the required majority, according to ScanX. Remote voting ran from October 8 through November 6, with the scrutiny report treating the resolution as passed on the final voting day.

A total of 12,822 members exercised voting rights, representing 10,257,377,196 shares. Institutional investors recorded 1.36 percent dissent, while non-institutional investors recorded 0.48 percent dissent. The voting pattern points to broad approval of the leadership change, although the different dissent levels show that shareholder groups were not completely aligned.

The vote settles a governance question that had remained relevant during the transition from Sashidhar Jagdishan. With the appointment approved, the focus shifts from succession to execution. Investors will assess whether Bagchi can improve growth, asset quality and profitability while maintaining the bank's competitive position in India's financial system.

HDFC Bank stock traded at 23.10 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 09:21 CET on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. The quote provides the latest European-market indication for the security; the shareholder vote, rather than the intraday price, is the central development for investors in this report.
For the broader market backdrop, see current S&P 500 market reports.

Further developments will center on Bagchi's execution agenda and the bank's operating performance. More news and analyses on HDFC Bank stock will track the leadership transition and its implications for investors.

Reliance Industries shares: Another record! RIL biggest on MTF book with 60% jump; dethrones HDFC Bank | Buy or sell?
sum: According to the latest data released by the National Stock Exchange (NSE) on November 2, Reliance Industries' MTF exposure jumped 60% to ₹4,711 crore, compared with ₹2,937 crore recorded at the end of October 30.
With this sharp increase, Reliance Industries has overtaken HDFC Bank to claim the top position in the MTF book, which the private lender had held for several months.

The overall MTF book stood at ₹1.45 lakh crore, with the top 10 stocks accounting for an exposure of ₹19,442 crore. Following Monday's surge, Reliance Industries alone accounted for 24% of the total exposure among these top 10 stocks.

Reliance Industries also continued to be the most traded stock in the Nifty 500 index on both Monday and Tuesday. Its trading turnover exceeded ₹11,000 crore on Monday and remained above ₹5,000 crore on Tuesday. Tuesday's session also witnessed delivery-based buying worth nearly ₹3,000 crore, following purchases of more than ₹6,000 crore in delivery volumes on Monday.
On November 2, Reliance Industries share price surged nearly 11.6% in a single session, accompanied by an extraordinary volume breakout.

“The stock has decisively broken above a prolonged downward sloping trendline, suggesting that selling pressure may finally be giving way to fresh buying interest. The confluence of a technical breakout, exceptional volumes, improving earnings and value unlocking through Jio makes Reliance an interesting stock to watch,” said Apurva Sheth, Head of Market Perspectives and Research, SAMCO Securities.

RIL posted a consolidated profit after tax (PAT), including its share of associates and joint ventures, of ₹29,550 crore in Q2 FY27, registering a 33.8% year-on-year (YoY) growth from ₹22,092 crore in the same quarter last year. Profit attributable to the company's owners surged 40% YoY to ₹25,548 crore.

Massive surge! Reliance Industries shares up 12% after Q2; add ₹2 lakh cr in mcap — when did RIL last rally this much?
sum: The shares finished Monday’s trade with a solid 12% jump to settle at ₹1,300 on NSE, their highest level since early September. The stock last posted a comparable single-day surge in April 2020. Given its heavyweight status in the Nifty 50, the rally also lifted the index by 1.7%, even as tensions in West Asia remained elevated.

For long-term Reliance Industries shareholders, the sharp rise has revived confidence in the stock, which had been trending lower since the start of 2026. The shares closed in the red in eight of the previous 10 months. Despite Monday’s rebound, the stock remains down 17.22% so far this year.

The double-digit jump in the stock added ₹1.84 lakh crore to the company’s market capitalisation, taking it to ₹17.6 lakh crore and helping it retain its position as India’s most valuable listed company.

At its peak of ₹1,611, the company commanded a market capitalisation of ₹21.8 lakh crore. It had crossed the ₹21 lakh crore mark in June 2024, becoming the first Indian company to achieve this milestone.

Meanwhile, investors in the Reliance Group have another reason to celebrate, as its telecom arm, Jio Platforms, made a blockbuster stock market debut last week, listing at ₹1,440 apiece, a premium of 21.3% over its issue price.

Reliance Industries Ltd reported a record consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of ₹29,550 crore for the July-September quarter (Q2 FY27), marking a 33.8% increase from ₹22,092 crore in the year-ago period. Revenue rose 27.8% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹3,62,268 crore, while EBITDA increased 23.9% to a record ₹62,409 crore.

The strong performance was primarily driven by a recovery in the oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business, where EBITDA surged 67.9% to ₹25,203 crore, supported by higher global fuel margins and improved petrochemical spreads. O2C revenue increased 44.2% to ₹2,31,601 crore, with supply disruptions in West Asia and other regions pushing transportation fuel cracks higher.

Jio Platforms vs Bharti Airtel shares: Which telecom stock to buy after Reliance arm’s IPO listing? Experts suggestions
sum: The listing of Jio Platforms has put the spotlight on India’s telecom sector, with investors now weighing whether the newly listed Reliance Industries-backed company or established rival Bharti Airtel offers a better investment opportunity.

Jio Platforms shares have surged nearly 28% from their issue price of ₹1,119 since making their market debut on Wednesday, 28 October, taking its market capitalisation to nearly ₹13.18 lakh crore and making it India’s second-most valuable listed company after Reliance Industries. The strong debut and subsequent gains follow an IPO that attracted bids for 22.19 times the shares on offer.

Bharti Airtel, meanwhile, has built a strong long-term track record, with its shares delivering returns of 586.10% over the past decade and 187.07% over five years. However, the stock remains down 6.64% so far in 2026. With Jio commanding a substantial valuation and Airtel offering an established earnings track record, which telecom stock should investors consider now? Experts weigh in on their growth prospects, valuations and investment appeal.

Bharti Airtel, meanwhile, remains a stronger proposition for investors seeking earnings visibility, higher ARPU, robust cash flows and disciplined capital allocation. Experts say investors should weigh valuations, earnings growth and execution risks before choosing between the two telecom stocks.

Gaurav Arora, Head of Research at SAHI, said Jio’s listing at a valuation of around ₹10.3 lakh crore places it among India’s top five companies by market capitalisation from day one. This, he said, changes the investment question from assessing the company’s growth potential to evaluating the returns investors can realistically expect from current levels. Companies of this scale rarely grow significantly faster than the broader economy, making low double-digit annual returns a reasonable base case.

He also noted that ARPU growth in India has historically been uneven, with increases largely coming through tariff hikes in 2019, 2021 and 2024. These hikes have typically required coordinated moves by all three telecom operators and have depended on regulatory considerations, making it difficult to factor in consistent ARPU growth over a 10-year investment horizon.

Shares of leading Indian private-sector banks slump 5% on weak earnings in June quarter
sum: Stocks of India's largest private lender HDFC Bank, along with those of Axis Bank, fell nearly 5% on Monday as concerns mounted over their weak net interest margins.
HDFC's NIM contracted 13 basis points sequentially to 3.4% from 3.53% in the last quarter. Axis Bank's NIMs compressed 16 basis points from a quarter ago to 3.46% in April-June.
"NIM compression, with softer fees" added to "earnings headwinds," Citigroup said in a report on Sunday, adding that NIMs will remain a "key monitorable" going ahead.
Shares of HDFC Bank have been under pressure since March, after Atanu Chakraborty, its part‑time chairman, resigned, flagging governance and ethical concerns within the institution.
In June, the bank said an independent legal review found no evidence to substantiate concerns raised in Chakraborty's resignation letter.
The global brokerage also noted that loan momentum has improved from the Mumbai-based lender, mostly led by demand from the commercial and corporate sector.
"Retail [loan] traction remained underwhelming," the report said.

sum: The Nifty Bank index rose to 58,376, gaining nearly 1%. The index snapped a two-session losing streak today.

HDFC Bank shares were the top gainers on the index, jumping nearly 3% after India's largest private lender reported gross advances at Rs 30.61 lakh crore at the end of the April-June quarter of FY27, marking a 15.4% year-on-year (YoY) rise from Rs 26.53 lakh crore reported in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. Its period end deposits meanwhile rose 14.7% YoY to Rs 31.71 lakh crore at the end of the first quarter of FY27, as against Rs 27.64 lakh crore reported at the end of the corresponding quarter of FY26.

JM Financial noted that HDFC Bank reported healthy deposit mobilisation. “HDFC Bank reported robust loan growth, marginally ahead of estimates, while deposit growth was in line. Consequently, the CD ratio inched up to 95.8% (vs. 94.6% in Q4 FY26). We expect margins to contract slightly this quarter and, in our recent preview note, estimated a 2bp QoQ margin contraction,” said Motilal Oswal in its note.
Also read: HDFC Bank Q1 business update | Gross advances rise 15% to Rs 30.61 lakh crore
Axis Bank, Federal Bank, State Bank of India and Yes Bank shares gained up to 1%, as seen at 11 am.
Also read: Yes Bank shares gain after Q1 advances rise 18% to Rs 2.85 lakh crore, deposits up 14%

Bucking the trend, Kotak Mahindra Bank shares crashed 4%, significantly weighing on the Nifty Bank index. This came after the private lender announced that its net advances for the quarter which ended on June 30, 2026, rose more than 15% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 5.12 lakh crore, from Rs 4.45 lakh crore reported in the same period last year. Deposits meanwhile grew nearly 12% YoY to Rs 5.73 lakh crore during Q1 FY27, from Rs 5.13 lakh crore in Q1 FY26. Sequentially however, the growth in deposits was marginal at 0.1% QoQ from Rs 5.72 lakh crore in Q4 FY26.

sum: Banking stocks remained among the biggest drivers of Friday's sharp market rally, with the Bank Nifty index climbing 3 percent and all 14 of its constituents ending firmly in the green. Strong gains in heavyweight lenders such as HDFC Bank, Axis Bank, ICICI Bank and State Bank of India helped propel benchmark indices higher, as easing geopolitical tensions and a sharp decline in crude oil prices boosted investor sentiment.

At the end of the trading session, the Nifty Bank index was up 3 percent at 56,815, outperforming the benchmark Nifty 50, which gained 2 percent. The Nifty Private Bank index advanced 2.8 percent, while the Nifty PSU Bank index rose 2.7 percent, placing banking among the best-performing sectors of the day.

The rally was broad-based, with all 14 Bank Nifty constituents ending higher. HDFC Bank gained 3.7 percent and emerged among the top contributors to Nifty gains. AU Small Finance Bank led the banking index gains, surging 5.7 percent to Rs 1,018. IDFC First Bank gained 5.6 percent, while Punjab National Bank rose 3.8 percent.

Among other major lenders, Yes Bank climbed 3.6 percent, Canara Bank advanced 3.4 percent and Union Bank of India gained 3.3 percent. IndusInd Bank rose 3.1 percent, Axis Bank advanced 2.7 percent and featured among the top Nifty gainers. Bank of Baroda rose 2.6 percent. Kotak Mahindra Bank gained 2.7 percent, ICICI Bank added 1.8 percent, Federal Bank advanced 1.7 percent, and State Bank of India rose 1.6 percent.

The rally in banking shares came as investors cheered signs of a possible breakthrough in the US-Iran conflict. Reports suggesting progress towards a diplomatic settlement triggered a sharp rebound in global equities and improved risk appetite across emerging markets.

A key support for financial stocks came from the steep decline in crude oil prices. Brent crude, the global benchmark, fell around 5 percent to about $86.4 per barrel, hovering near a two-month low. Lower oil prices are generally viewed as positive for India's inflation outlook, current account balance and interest-rate trajectory, improving the operating environment for banks and other domestic-focused sectors.

sum: Shares of DCB Bank Ltd rose sharply on Wednesday, settling 7.48 per cent higher at Rs 187.45. Ashish Kila, Director at Perfect Group and CIO of Perfect Wealth, believes the private lender's stock looks attractive even at current levels, citing earnings growth and strong management pedigree.

"It's available below book value. Still, they have compounded profits at 25–30 per cent. RoE (return on equity) is close to 13–15 per cent. This is a bank which has a market capitalisation (m-cap) of Rs 6,000 crore, and the pedigree of the management is gold standard. I would not rank it any less than HDFC Bank in terms of pedigree. I see a long runway for this company to serve the MSME sector and keep growing," Kila told Business Today.

items.t: HDFC Bank Issues Notice for Transfer of Unclaimed Equity Shares to IEPF Authority
sum: HDFC Bank Limited has published a regulatory notice for the transfer of unclaimed equity shares to IEPF Authority, affecting dividends from FY2018-19 and Special Interim Dividend FY2019-20. The bank sent communications to affected shareholders on April 6, 2026, with a claim deadline of August 11, 2026. Shareholders can verify details on the bank's website and reclaim transferred assets through MCA's web form IEPF-5 process.
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.

HDFC Bank Limited has issued a comprehensive notice regarding the mandatory transfer of unclaimed equity shares to the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF) Authority, in compliance with regulatory requirements under the Companies Act, 2013.

The notice, dated April 7, 2026, was submitted to both BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited as part of the bank's regulatory obligations. Under Section 124(6) of the Companies Act, 2013, read with the Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority (Accounting, Audit, Transfer and Refund) Rules, 2016, the bank must transfer shares corresponding to unclaimed dividends for seven consecutive years.

The bank has sent specific communications to concerned shareholders whose unclaimed dividends and shares are liable for transfer to IEPF. Shareholders holding shares in physical form will receive new share certificates in lieu of their existing certificates, which will be automatically cancelled and rendered non-negotiable. For shares held in demat mode, the transfer will be executed through corporate action via depositories to the IEPF Authority's demat account established by the Central Government.
The transfer process varies based on the mode of shareholding:
- Physical Shares: New share certificates will be issued before transfer, with original certificates becoming automatically cancelled

HDFC Bank shares fall nearly 3% as SEBI likely reviewing ex-chairman's exit letter, Jefferies exits lender
sum: HDFC Bank shares declined 3 percent on Friday amid reports that markets regulator SEBI is reviewing the resignation letter of former part-time chairman Atanu Chakraborty.
The stock fell after consecutive sessions of gains. It touched an intraday low of Rs 759.25 per share on the NSE, down 2.95 percent.

The decline follows reports that the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has initiated a preliminary review of Chakraborty’s resignation letter for possible violations of rules governing directors of listed companies, according to sources.
Chakraborty told Reuters he was not aware of any such examination by the regulator.
In his resignation letter, Chakraborty referred to "certain happenings and practices within the bank" which he said were "not in congruence" with his personal values and ethics. He did not elaborate.

Meanwhile, global brokerage Jefferies also exited its holdings in shares of private lender HDFC Bank, while trimming its India weightage, shortly after part-time chairman and independent director Atanu Chakraborty resigned from the board.
The stock had fallen 8.7 percent in the following session after the letter surfaced, eroding about Rs 1.35 lakh crore in market capitalisation over three sessions.

HDFC Bank has now extended its losses and is set for its worst week since March 2020. Bajaj Finance shares hit a new 52-week low of ₹787.90 today, and have now dropped 28.5% from their 52-week high of ₹1,102.50, recorded on October 23, last year. Shares of Bajaj Finserv are trading over 2% lower today after hitting the 52-week low of ₹1,665.90, which is 24% lower than its 52-week high of ₹2,195. Shares of Bajaj Finance have recovered sharply from the lows of the day. Shares of HDFC Life Insurance fell about 5% today to hit an intraday and 52-week low of ₹592.30, having dropped nearly 30% from its June 2025 highs of ₹820.75. The stock has dropped 20.35% this year, while delivering a negative 12.1% returns over the past 12 months. Shares of ITC Ltd. are trading nearly 3% lower today after hitting a 52-week low of ₹289.75. The stock has fallen 34.77% from its yearly high of ₹444.2 apiece. ITC shares have delivered a negative 28% return over the past 12 months. Shares of Hindustan Unilever Ltd , another FMCG company, also hit their 52-week low at ₹2,033.30 after falling over 26% from their 52-week high of ₹2,750. The stock has slipped more than 10% this year so far. IT stocks have also been hit by the crash, with Wipro and TCS hitting their respective 52-week lows at ₹187.3 and ₹2,348, respectively. Shares of Wipro fell 31.82% from their 52-week highs of ₹274.70, while those of TCS are down 36.71% from highs of ₹3,710 in March last year. Wipro has dropped 29.64% this year, while TCS is down 25.73% year-to-date. Shares of Ultratech are trading nearly 5% lower today, and at their 52-week low of ₹10,330.

HDFC Bank shares drop after chairman's exit. Should investors buy, sell or wait?
sum: HDFC Bank's fall has left investors at a crossroads. With strong fundamentals but lingering uncertainty, the big question now is simple: should you buy the dip, sell, or just wait?
Shares of HDFC Bank fell around 5% on Thursday after the sudden resignation of its part-time chairman Atanu Chakraborty, triggering concerns among investors and weighing on sentiment.

The stock slipped to around Rs 800 levels on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), underperforming the broader market, as the development added a layer of uncertainty around one of India’s most widely held banking stocks.

Chakraborty stepped down with immediate effect, citing issues related to “values and ethics” in his resignation letter. While he did not elaborate, the language used has drawn attention on Dalal Street.
The sharp reaction is less about immediate business impact and more about uncertainty.

Sudden exits at the top, especially when linked to internal practices, tend to make investors cautious. In this case, the lack of detailed explanation has left room for speculation, which markets typically dislike.
The bank and regulators have moved quickly to calm concerns.
